title: Sarah, an AI employee that answers the phone
excerpt: Scoping, architecting and building a voice agent that qualifies and books leads for home-services contractors, owned end to end.

metrics.label: Multi-tenant schema, one database for every contractor
Real voice cost against the first estimate, found in the model before any code
Jobber, Google and Meta connected from the first release

content:
01 · Discover

Requirements and scope

The first release was cut into two modules a contractor can switch on separately.

  • Module A, Reviews: post-sale review collection, AI-drafted SEO review replies, review-to-social content, automated referral asks
  • Module B, Leads: instant SMS outreach, AI voice call lead qualification and booking

Two approvals with long review times, Google Business Profile API allow-listing and Meta app review, were started on day one so they would not block launch.

02 · Architect

System design and cost

Everything runs on Cloudflare Workers with D1 for tenants, leads and reviews and KV for sessions, behind a 16-table multi-tenant schema. Calls come in through Twilio, the conversation runs on Vapi, and qualified leads are booked straight into Jobber.

The cheapest bug to fix was the pricing one, because it was found in a spreadsheet, not in production.

Modelling real per-call voice costs before writing code moved the estimate from five to ten cents a call to roughly fifty cents to $1.40 all in. Module pricing and call limits were reworked before the build started.

03 · Build

Implementation

A deployable Worker repo with the Twilio and Vapi integrations and the Jobber, Google and Meta OAuth flows, with the D1 database and KV namespace already provisioned.

04 · Launch

Not yet, on purpose

Launch waits on the platform approvals and a pilot with real contractors.

05–06 · Maintain and evolve

Roadmap and change log

Every change goes through one list: what it costs, what it touches, which release it lands in.
